facts.statement: Diplognathus lived during the Late Famennian stage of the Devonian period.
The genus Diplognathus was first described by Newberry in 1878.
Diplognathus mirabilis is the type species of the genus Diplognathus.
Two species are currently recognized within the genus: D. mirabilis and D. larfargei.
facts.quote: subdivision: *D. mirabilis Newberry, 1878 D. larfargei Carr, 2005

facts.statement: Fossils of Diplognathus have been found in the Cleveland Shale of Ohio, dating to the Late Devonian.
facts.quote: Diplognathus is a genus of arthrodire placoderm from the Late Famennian Cleveland Shale of Late Devonian Ohio

facts.statement: The known fossil record of Diplognathus consists only of incomplete fragments of jaws and skulls.
facts.quote: known only from incomplete fragments of jaws and skulls

facts.statement: Evidence suggests that Diplognathus were large-eyed fish-eaters with weak but widely gaping jaws.
facts.quote: What fragments are known suggest that the living animals were large-eyed piscivores with weak, but widely gaping jaws

facts.statement: Diplognathus mirabilis is considered fairly large, with lower jaws reaching up to 45 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: D. mirabilis is thought to be fairly large, with infragnathals up to 45 centimeters in length

facts.statement: Diplognathus larfargei was much smaller than D. mirabilis, with lower jaws averaging about 4 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: The second species, D. larfargei, was much smaller, with inferognathals averaging about 4 centimeters in length

facts.statement: In 1967, Obruchev classified the genus Diplognathus within the family Hadrosteidae.
facts.quote: In 1967, Obruchev placed this genus within Hadrosteidae

facts.statement: It is debated whether Diplognathus belongs in Hadrosteidae, as Denison contested this placement in 1978 and preferred to classify it as Arthrodira incertae sedis.
facts.quote: though Denison (1978) contested this placement, preferring to leave the taxon as Arthrodira incertae sedis

facts.statement: Diplognathus belongs to the parent group Arthrodira.
Diplognathus is classified within the class Placodermi.
